summary: Checks whether a value is a rich text value.
description: An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "RichTextValue"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a rich text value; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
const value = SpreadsheetApp.newRichTextValue().setText("a").build();

isRichTextValue(value); // => true
isRichTextValue({}); // => false
isRichTextValue(null); // => false
```
